=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:9700-9706 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: runner_lost_failure() classifies a job as runner-lost when any single annotation matches the shutdown regex (line 9704), ignoring annotation_level and without requiring all failure annotations to be shutdown-class.
  WHY: A job with a real failure annotation alongside a shutdown annotation, or a PR step that emits matching `::error::` text, gets dropped with skip reason=runner_lost and the real failure is never filed (severity ranged NIT to MAJOR across reviewers; highest used).
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1818 | severity=major | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The annotations request uses the Actions job ID (scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:9673-9685) as the check-run ID instead of parsing it from job["check_run_url"].
  WHY: If the two IDs differ, the read 404s or reads an unrelated check run, so lost-droplet failures are filed anyway. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 dissented: the check-run ID equals the job ID for Actions jobs, so it dropped the finding.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1818 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: gh_api_json_to_file retries each annotations read up to 5 times (GH_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS default), across up to 10 candidate jobs.
  WHY: This can reach about 50 requests and about 150 s of backoff, exceeding the documented "at most 10 reads" budget (severity NIT to MAJOR across reviewers; highest used; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 called it a documentation nit only).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "ci.yml, workflow_failure_heal.yml and check_failure_triage.yml never read it, so the repair path never depends on the fleet"; the README and changelog say the heal path always stays on GitHub-hosted runners.
  expected_change_site: heal-report jobs in .github/workflows/clarify.yml:2546, .github/workflows/implement.yml:7382, .github/workflows/plan.yml:4000, .github/workflows/validate.yml:1946
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: All four heal-report jobs use the PIPELINE_RUNS_ON do-runner expression, tests/test_pipeline_runs_on_switch.py only exempts ci.yml, workflow_failure_heal.yml and check_failure_triage.yml, and a broken droplet fleet would stop failures from being reported to the heal intake. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 judged this a NIT (confidence 2): the PR says every job of the 17 reusable workflows is routed, so only the README wording is unclear.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1818 | severity=nit | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The shared retry helper can multiply the 10-reads-per-run budget (hardening suggestion; documentation drift only).
  WHY: Suggested fix: say "at most 10 reads, each retried by the shared helper" in the comment, README.md and agents.d.
- TASK_GAP:
  Requirement: "`ci.yml`, `workflow_failure_heal.yml` and `check_failure_triage.yml` never read it, so the repair path never depends on the fleet."
  Expected change site: the `heal-report` jobs in clarify.yml (~2546), implement.yml (~7382), plan.yml (~4000), validate.yml (~1946)
  Evidence of absence: The PR says every job of the 17 reusable workflows is routed, so routing the heal-report jobs matches the stated deliverable. The README could say more clearly that heal-report reporter jobs follow PIPELINE_RUNS_ON.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- Dropped pass-1 findings (not reported): the job ID versus check-run ID claim, and annotation matching without annotation_level.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  PROBLEM: The decision ignores annotation_level and trusts the raw message.
  WHY: A failing consumer step could emit an `::error::` annotation matching the shutdown regex, suppressing the heal issue.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:9704 | severity=major | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The lost-runner decision trusts the raw annotation message at any level, without the three guards that scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py:385-389, 435-437 and 441-446 apply.
  WHY: A PR step emitting `::error::The runner has received a shutdown signal` can suppress a real heal issue.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1818 | severity=major | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: ${lost_job_id} is the Actions job ID, but check-runs/{id}/annotations needs the check-run ID (see scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py:99, 431 and scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:603-605).
  WHY: The read 404s or reads another check run, so the runner-lost skip never fires, and the mock gh in tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:2046 mirrors the wrong ID.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:9700-9706 | severity=major | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A job qualifies as runner-lost when any one annotation matches, even if it also carries a real failure annotation.
  WHY: The run is dropped at scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1821-1824 and the real failure is not filed, contradicting the documented fail-open contract.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1818 | severity=major | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: gh_api_json_to_file retries up to GH_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 5), for up to 10 candidate jobs.
  WHY: Up to 50 requests and about 150 s of sleep in a heal job break the documented bound (the same file bounds a comparable read at scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:2934).
- TASK_GAP:
  Requirement: "ci.yml, workflow_failure_heal.yml and check_failure_triage.yml never read it, so the repair path never depends on the fleet"; the README says the heal and triage workflows always stay on GitHub-hosted runners.
  Expected change site: the heal-report jobs at clarify.yml:2546, plan.yml:4000, validate.yml:1946, implement.yml:7382
  Evidence of absence: The four jobs are switched to the do-runner expression and no test pins them to a GitHub-hosted runner, so with a dead fleet no report reaches the intake.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:9673-9685; scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1818 | severity=major | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The candidate helper returns Actions job IDs and the intake uses them as check-run IDs, not the job's check_run_url.
  WHY: When the IDs differ, the request reads the wrong check run or 404s, and the infrastructure failure is filed as a heal issue.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:9688-9706 | severity=major | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: runner_lost_failure() classifies a job as lost when any annotation matches the shutdown pattern, without requiring all failure annotations to match or checking annotation_level.
  WHY: A job with both a shutdown and a real failure annotation is classified as runner-lost, hiding the real failure.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1818 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The annotations GET uses gh_api_json_to_file without GH_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=1, and the helper defaults to five attempts.
  WHY: Up to 50 requests with backoff exceed the documented 10-read limit and can eat much of the 10-minute timeout.
- TASK_GAP:
  Requirement: "The repair path never depends on the fleet"; the README and changelog say the heal path stays on GitHub-hosted runners.
  Expected change site: heal-report jobs in clarify.yml, implement.yml, plan.yml, validate.yml
  Evidence of absence: All four heal-report jobs use the PIPELINE_RUNS_ON expression, so the phase failure report may not reach the intake if the fleet is down.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:9700-9706 (regex at lines 484-487) | severity=major | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The lost-runner decision accepts any matching annotation with no annotation_level filter, uses .search() substring matching, and does not require other failure annotations to be absent (compare scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py:385-389, 435-437).
  WHY: A PR step or a real exit-code annotation alongside a shutdown annotation leads to skip reason=runner_lost (scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1893-1895) and a real failure is never filed.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1818 | severity=major | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The annotations request uses the job ID as the check-run ID rather than deriving it from check_run_url (scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py:431, scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:598-605).
  WHY: If the IDs differ, the read 404s or reads another check run, so lost-droplet failures are filed anyway, and tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:2550 bakes in the equality assumption.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1818 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A permanently failing annotations read is retried 5 times per candidate job (scripts/gh_helpers.sh:2378, 2426-2432), for up to 10 jobs.
  WHY: Up to 50 calls and about 150 s of sleep inside a heal-report job with a 10-minute timeout, amplifying the documented 10-read budget 5x.
- TASK_GAP:
  Requirement: "`ci.yml`, `workflow_failure_heal.yml` and `check_failure_triage.yml` never read it, so the repair path never depends on the fleet."
  Expected change site: heal-report jobs in clarify.yml:2546, implement.yml:7382, plan.yml:4000, validate.yml:1946
  Evidence of absence: The four runs-on lines are switched to the do-runner expression and tests/test_pipeline_runs_on_switch.py:66-77 pins every non-`uses` job of a routed workflow to it, so with a broken fleet no ai:workflow-heal issue is filed.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
